- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce subsequent values by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If true price deviates from forecast by >10% in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days), check sentiment for reversal signals — if sentiment shifts, adjust forecast direction accordingly.
- Model often underestimates mean-reversion periods — if recent price is trending strongly, forecast should be more conservative toward mid-term.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth out extremes and anchor to 14-day moving average of history.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.33” values, model may be ignoring sentiment — force a slight upward bias if price is trending up, or downward if trending down.
